correctness.rationale: The geometry gives A=sum tan(pi Y_i) precisely on the bounded-event max Y_i<1/2; circular spacings are uniform Dirichlet. The exact simplex-strip density yields each tangent singular tail, and exact two-coordinate simplex translation bounds simultaneous extremes by O(t^{-(n-1)}) for n>=3. A deterministic maximum-to-sum sandwich yields the sharp coefficient; the tail-integral identity yields the strict q=1 integrability boundary. The calculation was independently spot-checked algebraically for n=3..12 and by finite Monte Carlo for n=3,4,6 (which is not used as proof). Boundaries and quantifiers are specified.

originality.rationale: The novelty candidate is the complete fixed-n asymptotic coefficient for the tail of area conditional on a bounded random circle-tangent polygon, and its sharp moment threshold. The 2015 same-model source acknowledges unbounded possible magnitudes, but its accessible abstract does not give this quantitative tail. The inspected 2023 full-text HTML states the tangent-gap representation and works with large-n laws. Fodor--Hug--Ziebarth (2014) treats a different random-halfspace model with outer clipping. Closest accessible published results address random rotation of fixed tangential bodies and random inscribed polygons. No equivalent or stronger fixed-n conditional Pareto-tail formula was located. The complete 2015 Xu article was inaccessible, so historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: Complete Xu (2015) text inaccessible; the exact fixed-n constant could have been treated in its proofs or appendices despite abstract silence.
Indexed mathematical literature, including older stochastic-geometry sources on circle tangent lines, is not exhaustive; independent historical-priority audit is needed.

value.rationale: Expected area is the natural estimation functional in random circumscribed polygon approximation. The conditioned model excludes the obvious unbounded-polyhedron outcomes, yet still lacks finite mean; the exact 1/t coefficient quantifies a rare but structurally unavoidable near-semicircle tangency mechanism for every sample size. This sharp integrability obstruction is mathematically informative when comparing finite-n geometry to large-n normal-approximation literature; the numeric constants depend nontrivially on n. No oversized downstream claim is needed.
